items.limitations_counterevidence_locator: Not Disclosed — exact-v1 has no dedicated limitations section; the review boundary is reconstructed from §4 Experiment, which only evaluates disclosed ASR, TTS, VQA and text-to-image workloads, and §5 Conclusion, which states potential rather than a production guarantee.
items.artifact_locator: arXiv:2603.06577v1 HTML abstract — project webpage https://omni-diffusion.github.io; no immutable code commit or released deployment artifact is disclosed in the exact-v1 used here.
items.problem_and_changed_constraint: Any-to-any multimodal understanding and generation need not inherit an autoregressive backbone. A mask-based discrete diffusion backbone can jointly model text, image and speech token targets, exposing parallel mutable positions and modality-dependent decoding policies across both training and inference.
items.mechanism_and_ownership: The paper extends Dream-7B with 8,192 image tokens and 16,384 speech tokens, uses modality-specific image and speech front/back ends, progressively aligns modalities in three stages, and applies entropy-based parallel decoding plus modality-specific position, pre-infill and length controls. The generator owns provisional masked-token state; modality tokenizers/decoders retain codec identity; the runtime still owns final commit.
items.evaluation_contract: The evidence covers Dream-7B-based experiments on disclosed ASR/TTS, VQA and text-to-image benchmarks, plus step-count sensitivity for text-to-image and TTS. Hardware, precision, production concurrency, end-to-end service latency, long-running multimodal dialogue reliability and immutable implementation revision are Not Disclosed.
items.claim_boundary: The source supports mask-based discrete diffusion as a viable any-to-any multimodal factorization under its disclosed model, modality adapters, data and benchmark contracts. It does not prove one coherent tokenizer/decoder across modalities, universal superiority to autoregression, semantic correctness from fewer denoising steps, or production SLO gains.
items.tradeoff_failure_and_coexistence: Joint masked-token modeling reuses one backbone and exposes parallel generation, but preserves modality-specific codecs, requires progressive alignment, and adds generation-order, initial-length and provisional-state errors. Autoregressive or specialist-head systems remain valid where sequential commit, hard typed output, calibration or deployment simplicity dominate.

items.artifact_locator: Not Disclosed — exact-v1 does not expose a public ReGT dataset or immutable evaluation-code revision. Bibliographic links to third-party software are not the reviewed experiment artifact.
items.problem_and_changed_constraint: Model rankings and capability conclusions can reverse when dataset labels, output mapping, distractor construction, response format, batch size, image order, batch composition or mapping encoder change. Those are evaluation identity, not incidental script details.
items.mechanism_and_ownership: The paper evaluates Closed-World, CW+ nearest-neighbor mapping, Multiple-Choice and Open-World protocols under reannotated multilabel ReGT. Dataset owner controls label and annotation provenance; harness owner controls prompt, batching, ordering and response format; mapping encoder and rule are part of scorer identity; release interpretation must consume their joint version.
items.evaluation_contract: The study covers five named MLLMs on ImageNet-1k, ReGT for 625 classes, protocol ablations, and 31 repeats for GPT-4o at temperature zero. It observes strong sensitivity for some models, including LLaVA-OV batch/position effects, random-versus-grouped batch bias, response-format changes, mapping-encoder changes and distractor difficulty. ReGT is not public and excluded many fine-grained wildlife categories; the model-assisted annotation workflow can itself bias labels.
items.claim_boundary: The source supports the conclusion that the reported MLLM classification comparison is conditional on a versioned dataset, label policy, task formulation, prompt/output mapping, distractor policy, batch/order/composition and mapping encoder. It does not prove corrected labels are final truth, that the measured deltas transfer beyond the disclosed models and ImageNet slices, or that MLLMs generally match supervised classifiers.
items.tradeoff_failure_and_coexistence: Richer relabeling and protocol decomposition improve attribution but increase annotation cost, mapping-model dependence and degrees of freedom. Strict exact-match and fixed batches remain useful reproducible baselines when their bias is acknowledged; open-world mapping is preferable only when the mapping encoder and calibration are frozen and audited.

books_comparison.decision_reason: The target chapter states the general identity contract but does not yet make batch size, image position/order, batch composition, response format, output mapping, mapping encoder and distractor construction explicit as jointly versioned evaluation state. The source also provides a correction case where these hidden knobs and label provenance alter the conclusion.
books_comparison.proposed_owner_delta: When one request contains multiple samples or a free-form model output is mapped into benchmark labels, EvalRun identity must include batch size, within-batch order and composition, response schema, out-of-vocabulary handling, mapping encoder/revision and distractor-construction policy. Dataset relabeling must preserve annotator inputs and model-assistance provenance. Changing any of these creates a new result lineage; it cannot silently repair or compare the old score.
